correctness.rationale: Every cyclic factor of length at most n contains 0, 1, or 2 ones. The proof explicitly lists all palindromes in these three disjoint cases, subtracts the duplicate family when the two zero gaps agree, and derives the parity spectrum from floor identities. It counts rotation orbits of sizes n or n/2 to obtain the complete labeled distribution and exact rational moments. The bundled standalone checker directly enumerated 1,510 gap instances and compared all 44 finite distributions and moments. These checks corroborate, but do not replace, the exhaustive all-length combinatorial proof.

originality.rationale: Comparison is by implication. The classical general bound a general \(5n/3\) upper bound does not determine the exact three-stratum fixed-weight-two spectrum or the vanishing-versus-linear parity variance. The published global-maxima table records extrema at individual lengths, not all sparse circular words. A subsequent accessible article concerns squares instead of palindromes. Separate semantic searches and accessible prior claims did not reveal an equivalent. The full 2014 primary paper remained inaccessible; an uninspected explicit special case remains a named priority risk, so this is best-knowledge originality only.

value.rationale: The layer of binary circles with exactly two marked positions is a natural first nontrivial sparse layer in circular-palindrome extremal theory. An all-length *complete* gap and orbit classification reveals a nonobvious parity rigidity: at every odd length all such circles have identical palindrome counts, whereas even-length variance is asymptotically \(n/16\) due to a unique, rare antipodal configuration. It supplies exact multiplicities and sampling moments rather than an arbitrary short finite table or a generic bound. The value does not depend on claiming a new unrestricted extremal result.
